memory_update.text: TreeHouse Foods was the cleanest US public private-label food-manufacturing comp, but it completed a take-private transaction on February 11, 2026; future Layer 1 work should not treat THS as an active listed candidate.

SENEA and JBSS are the strongest underfollowed US-listed direct candidates found in this pass because both disclose private-label/private-brand or contract-manufacturing exposure and sit behind retailer/CPG brands.

GPK is a packaging reference candidate, not a pure private-label name; use it to benchmark packaging capacity, fiber-based formats, food/beverage packaging demand and retail-ready packaging economics.

FARM is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate with direct private-label coffee language, but it fails the preferred market-cap filter and needs liquidity, balance-sheet and customer-mix verification before surviving later layers.

For this node, the most testable chokepoint signals are food-safety certification, retailer qualification, plant utilization, commodity pass-through, packaging substrate availability, seasonal crop supply, and top-customer concentration.

node: Private-label co-manufacturing, specialty ingredients, labels, flexible packaging, and shelf-ready packaging
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the private-label supply bottleneck. The strongest underfollowed lane is not the visible retailer but behind-the-label manufacturers with food-safety, processing, packaging, retailer qualification, and seasonal/raw-material constraints. TreeHouse Foods would have been the obvious public reference pure-play, but it completed a take-private acquisition in February 2026, so the investable US-listed screen shifts toward smaller packaged-food processors, ingredient/private-brand suppliers, and packaging vendors. No buy/sell view is provided.
